name: D-Ribose-L-cysteine
lead: D-Ribose-L-cysteine (DRLC), sold under the names RiboCeine and RibCys, is a patented synthetic compound intended to deliver L-cysteine to cells and so support the body's own glutathione production [1]. Glutathione is a cellular antioxidant, and cysteine availability is described as the limiting factor in making it [1].

According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference, it was developed in the 1990s by Herbert T. Nagasawa at a Veterans Affairs medical center and the University of Minnesota, with patents assigned to Max International and the US Department of Veterans Affairs [1]. It is catalogued in longevity circles rather than appearance communities. Published work found is preclinical; no human clinical study of it was found.

paras: Grokipedia describes DRLC as a thiazolidine formed by condensing D-ribose with L-cysteine, a ring structure said to protect the thiol group from oxidation, which is a stated limitation of free cysteine [1].

Proponents describe DRLC as a prodrug that releases cysteine inside cells, raising glutathione synthesis; one claim in the reference is that it raised glutathione more than N-acetylcysteine in a cell-culture hepatocyte study [1]. These descriptions come from a non-peer-reviewed source and originate largely with the product's developers and patent holders.

No studies found in humans. Related laboratory and animal work includes a study of ribose-cysteine on glutathione-based antioxidant status and LDL in lipoprotein(a) transgenic mice [2], and an experimental study of ribose-cysteine pretreatment on acetaminophen metabolite formation and glutathione depletion in liver and kidney [3]. A combined-antioxidant trial in mice examined age-related hearing loss [4]. A registered phase II breast cancer trial appears in a trial search for the compound, but its role in that study is not described in the material reviewed [5].

card.summary: A patented cysteine prodrug marketed to raise glutathione; research is preclinical and nothing covers appearance.
card.note: Supporting claims come largely from developer-linked and animal or cell studies.

quick.overview:
D-Ribose-L-cysteine is a branded supplement ingredient designed to supply cysteine for glutathione, the body's main cellular antioxidant. It is mentioned in longevity contexts.

Published research is limited to cell and animal studies; no human trial was found and none addresses looks.
quick.mechanism: The ribose-cysteine ring is described as resisting oxidation until the cell releases cysteine, which the body uses to synthesise glutathione.
quick.risks: No human safety data were found in the sources reviewed. Claims of superiority over N-acetylcysteine rest on cell-culture and animal work described by a non-peer-reviewed reference.
